bank_plan.formula: (lesson_check_items + module_check_items) x 2 alternates + forms x form_length
bank_plan.eighty_twenty_note: 80% instruction / 20% assessment honoured at course level (I+A=T); bank serves lesson checks, module checks, 3 practice forms and a protected final.
bank_plan.size_band_note: Planning range per assessment standard (200-600 skills; 600-1500+ large certification). This is a planning guide, not proof of quality.

mcq_limitation_note: Official test assesses writing and speaking; MCQ/MR cannot assess productive skills. Mastemy teaches all four skills by video and model-answer analysis but scores only receptive and knowledge items.

items.stem: A speaker says 'The meeting is on Tuesday... sorry, I mean Thursday.' The answer box asks for the day. What is correct?

options.rationale: Correct: the self-correction replaces Tuesday with Thursday, the final stated answer.
Tuesday was corrected and is no longer the intended answer.
Only the corrected day is the answer; listing both is wrong.
The corrected day Thursday is clearly the intended answer.

items.explanation: Self-corrections replace the earlier information; take the final stated value.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: A completion answer must be 'ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER'. The spoken answer is 'twenty pounds'. What should be written if only the amount is required and the symbol is pre-printed?

options.rationale: Correct: a number counts as allowed, and the currency symbol is already printed, so '20' fits the limit.
That is two words and exceeds a one-word/number limit.
Writing the word omits the numeric amount expected and may mis-match the pre-printed symbol.
Adding 'pounds' exceeds the limit when the symbol is pre-printed.

items.explanation: Respect the word/number limit and the pre-printed units.

items.stem: Which TWO strategies most help in Section 4 (a lecture)?

options.text: Using signpost language to anticipate upcoming answers
options.rationale: Correct: lectures are heavily signposted, aiding prediction.

options.text: Reading ahead to the next questions while listening
options.rationale: Correct: Section 4 runs without a mid-section pause, so reading ahead is essential.

options.text: Waiting for the answer to be repeated
options.rationale: Answers are usually said once; waiting risks missing them.

options.text: Writing full sentences for every point
options.rationale: Full sentences are too slow and unnecessary.
Question wording guides what to listen for.

items.explanation: Signpost tracking and reading ahead fit Section 4's continuous delivery.
